The file Cslib/Foundations/Semantics/LTS/Basic.lean is now over 1000 lines long and is getting a bit unwieldy. I propose that it be split into the following files:

  • LTS/Execution.lean: the code about LTS.Execution and LTS.OmegaExecution (see cslib#449).
  • LTS/Total.lean: the code in the section Total.
  • LTS/HasTau.lean: the code in the sections Weak and Divergence.
  • LTS/Basic.lean: all remaining code excluding the above.

In addition to make the individual files easier to deal with, such a split will also make the LTS dependencies from different parts of cslib more granular. What do you think?

This work should wait until cslib#449 and cslib#444 are merged.
I am absolutely in favor. Also seems like a good time for this to help in diagnosing the performance issues the LTS scope has.
Me too, it's long due. Plus there's some refactoring coming from downstream. Let me get around cslib#449 and cslib#444 first and I'll come back here for coordinating this together.
(Going through all the PRs that risk being broken by this change first... almost done.)
I also would like to change some Prop definitions to structures, but I'll hold off until after the split to make things easier. For LTS.Execution especially, this makes things much nicer.
Thanks for merging cslib#449 and cslib#444. I'll get on with the splitting work.

I'm getting a very weird error after I put the section Total in its own file Total.lean. The section contains the following definition:

def LTS.totalize (lts : LTS State Label) : LTS (State ⊕ Unit) Label where
  Tr s' μ t' := match s', t' with
    | inl s, inl t => lts.Tr s μ t
    | _, inr () => True
    | inr (), inl _ => False

After I put it in its own file, Lean produces the following error message:

Invalid pattern: Expected a constructor or constant marked with [match_pattern]

even though I do have open Sum at the beginning of the file. The error would go away only after I replace each inl or inr by Sum.inl and Sum.inr. Anyone has an idea what's going on?
